Brief Hospital Course:
ASSESSMENT
The patient is a ___ year-old man with a history of multiple 
abdominal surgeries with chronic pain, DVTs, PEs, a questionable 
family history of factor V leiden, and a history of drug-seeking 
behavior who presents with pleuritic chest pain and LLQ 
abdominal pain.
.
CHEST PAIN
The patient presents with pleuritic chest pain that changes with 
position. There was concern for a PE, pericarditis, MI, or 
pneumonia. Also, the patient had not been taking his lovenox for 
the past week. The CXR and CT scans show no evidence of PE, EKG 
was unremarkable, and the patient has no calf edema or pain. His 
cardiac enzymes were negative x2. These results make PE or MI 
very unlikely. He claims to have a history of 6 DVT/PE episodes. 
It is unlikely that he has pericarditis since his pain does not 
improve with leaning forward and his EKG did not show diffuse ST 
elevations. Also, he probably does not have a pneumonia since 
his cough is non-productive, his CXR is clear, and his WBC count 
is consistent with his baseline values. He may be having a viral 
syndrome that could be causing some pleural inflammation, but 
the major problems listed above were ruled out. Included in his 
differential is his history of frequent hospitalizations for 
various complaints consistent with negative findings in past. 
His pain was treated with diclofenac + PPI. No opiates were 
given in setting of his history of abusing medications. See 
below.
.
ABDOMINAL PAIN
The patient has LLQ pain that presented with his chest pain. He 
reports a history of pancreatitis and diverticulitis and 
adhesions. A recent colonoscopy at ___ did not 
show any significant abnormalities. CT scan of abdomen and 
pelvis were unremarkable. As per ___ records, the 
patient underwent and endoscopy and small bowel follow through 
in ___, both of which were negative. CT scan did show a small 
right anterolateral wall hernia. He has had chronic abdominal 
pain issues in the past few years, but has not had adequate pain 
control. Patient was recommended to follow-up at the chronic 
pain clinic.
.
HISTORY OF DVT AND PE
Patient reports history of 6 DVT/PE events. In ___, 
patient was admitted to ___ had a CT angiogram of 
his chest that was read as recurrent pulmonary embolus.  
However, he was transferred to ___ and the CT was reread and 
there was no evidence of PE. He was on coumadin at this time, 
but was non-compliant with coumadin and lab draws. He was 
adivised stop Coumadin and was put on Lovenox on ___ for 
ease of monitoring. His last PE was on ___ per OSH records. 
He was admitted to ___ with left-sided chest pain 
and was found to have a left lower lobe PE on chest CT. He was 
given weight-based treatment doses of Lovenox and currently 
takes 100 mg twice per day. He has not taken his Lovenox in the 
past week. During this admission, he was changed to Lovenox ___ 
mg once daily, as high treatment doses were not indicated. This 
one time dose also improves ease of administration.
.
CHRONIC PAIN
The patient has had multiple abdominal surgical procedures and 
receives care at 4 different hospitals. He states that his pain 
is poorly controlled, especially in the past few years. He has a 
past history of drug seeking behavior and OSH records document 
""doctor shopping"" and pain medication abuse. He has a h/o pain 
medication contract at ___. He currently states that he unable 
to find a primary doctor and seeks a long term and consistent 
relationship with a physician. Patient did not receive any 
prescriptions for opiates given his history of medication abuse. 
He was recommended to seek care at ___ and was given a 
new appointment at ___.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted with chest pain and abdominal pain. You had a 
CT of your chest and abdomen that showed no abnormalities and no 
evidence of PE. You had no problems with your heart. There is a 
small adrenal mass that was seen previously and is unchanged and 
does not require follow-up.
.
You will continue your lovenox but at a smaller dose; it is

radiology_notes.text:
CLINICAL INDICATION:  ___ male with history of PE, presenting with
fever, evaluate for pneumonia.

___.

PA AND LATERAL CHEST:  The cardiomediastinal silhouette is stable.  The lungs
are clear.  There is no pleural effusion.  The pulmonary vasculature is
unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  No radiographic evidence of pneumonia.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  ___ man with history of PE and DVT, now off
Lovenox.

___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired images were obtained through the chest, abdomen, and
pelvis after the uneventful administration of 130 cc IV Optiray contrast.
Multiplanar reformats were reviewed.

CT CHEST:  There is no evidence of filling defect within the main pulmonary
arteries, although beyond the segmental level the evaluation is limited by
motion artifact.  There is no axillary, hilar, or mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
The lungs demonstrate variable attenuation due to microatelectasis secondary
to breathing. There is no pneumothorax or pleural effusion. 

CT ABDOMEN: The liver, splenectomy bed, and left adrenal gland are
unremarkable. The right adrenal gland demonstrates a subcentimeter nodule. The
kidneys are grossly unremarkable. There is no evidence of retroperitoneal or
mediastinal lymphadenopathy. There is a 2 cm ventral hernia with a narrow neck
extending to the subcutaneous tissues in the right upper quadrant (3b:154).

PELVIS:  The colon, urinary bladder, prostate and seminal vesicles are
unremarkable. the appendix is not well seen, although there are no secondary
signs of appendicitis.

Bone windows demonstrate no suspicious lytic or blastic lesions.

Subcutaneous air is noted in the right lower quadrant superficial abdominal
soft tissues may be related to recent injection.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No evidence of large PE with limited evaluation of levels including and
below the segmental arteries.

2.  No evidence of acute intra-abdominal pathology.

3.  Stable nodule in the right adrenal gland.

4.  Small anterior ventral right upper quadrant hernia.
